svg.aria-label: Three front ends over one flint bucket: flint-lite serves live shared POSIX from a hub pod over NFSv4.2; flint-lean materializes plain local files and publishes boundaries with a worker; flint-passthrough mounts an S3 prefix directly with Mountpoint for S3. All three read and write the same bucket, whose control namespace differs per front end.
svg.text: flint-lite — the hub
live shared POSIX, many readers AND writers
the consumer pod — any cluster
nothing from flint is installed in it
mount: /data (an ordinary PVC)
the node's KERNEL NFS client carries every byte —
one mount per node, pods share it and its page cache
full POSIX: byte-range locks, atomic rename, O_EXCL
flint-lite hub — ONE pod, one volume
flint-pnfs-mds · mode: standalone
:2049 NFSv4.2 — the data plane
:8080 status + file API — ClusterIP only
PVC = the working set + .flint-nfs/state.db
a CACHE of the bucket, never the only copy
single replica · Recreate · exclusive flock
coordination — the hub IS the authority
leases, locks and close-to-open are enforced in one
process, so every client sees one coherent tree
a second hub on the prefix is fenced by the epoch cell
publish · hydrate
RPO = the flush cadence
flint-lean — checkout / publish
one agent, one workspace, one writer
the agent pod
the app image is unchanged and holds no S3 credential
/workspace (local disk — an emptyDir)
PLAIN FILES. There is no interception anywhere in the
read or write path — this is just a local filesystem
so git, sqlite and build caches simply work, at disk speed
flint-sync — an unprivileged worker
delivered by the s3.csi.chert.us CSI driver
checkout at start — before the agent's first line
barrier at cadence — an mtime/size scan
boundary verbs: the agent writes .flint/publish,
the sidecar answers .flint/publish.ack
preStop drains — a graceful stop loses nothing
coordination — a lease in the BUCKET
one writer per subtree, admitted by a CAS on the epoch
cell; a second syncer is REFUSED, never merged
readers see the last published boundary, not the last write
checkout · publish
RPO = the last barrier
flint-passthrough — the mount
an S3 prefix, mounted as-is — no flint semantics
the tenant pod
no sidecar, no label, no credential, no privilege —
admissible under PodSecurity `restricted`
/mnt/s3 (a csi: volume naming a CR)
objects appear as files, served by Mountpoint for S3
NOT POSIX: no rename, no append, no in-place modification
s3.csi.chert.us — a CSI node DaemonSet
one privileged process per NODE, not per pod
it opens /dev/fuse and calls mount(2) itself
then hands the fd to an unprivileged worker pod
the worker runs an unchanged mount-s3 and needs no
privilege, because the mount already happened
the plugin holds NO S3 credential — a broker mints them
coordination — NONE, by design
no cache, no manifest, no publish boundary, and no
coordination whatsoever between pods sharing a prefix
S3's own consistency is the entire contract you get
GET · PUT
no RPO — there is nothing to flush
One bucket. One format. Three front ends — and a volume can move between them.
Whole-file objects plus a `.flint/` control namespace. The front end decides what that namespace contains; the bytes are the same bytes.
flint-lite writes
<prefix>/<path>
<prefix>.flint/epoch
<prefix>.flint/manifest
<prefix>.flint/owner
flint-lean writes
<prefix>/files/<path>
<prefix>/.flint/lean/epoch · claim
<prefix>/.flint/lean/current
<prefix>/.flint/lean/inbox
flint-passthrough writes
<prefix>/<key>
and nothing else. There is no control
namespace, because there is no state to
keep — it is somebody else's bucket layout.
Read the columns as an escalation ladder, cheapest first.

Passthrough asks nothing of the workload and gives it nothing back; lean gives real POSIX at local speed for one writer; the hub is the only one of the three that can make several pods share one live tree.
